A.notes: A hull 'draft marks' idea (seven movements stacked 07-to-01 like waterline marks, a tide bar on mobile, waterlines under each opener, a dark Monsoon movement) is carried through the whole piece. In the strips the draft gauge visibly fills section by section, so the motion marks structure without getting in the way of reading. The Newsreader and IBM Plex Mono pairing is restrained and very readable at 375px, with two-way footnotes, a skip link and a clean reduced-motion page, though the cover and openers are a bit austere and the light nav box on the dark Monsoon section looks slightly out of place.

B.notes: A polished magazine treatment: a deep-green cover with an italic 'Sadarghat', a wave rule, big rust numerals, 'Part one' labels and drop caps, set in a well-hyphenated column that reads comfortably on a phone. In the strips the reading bar updates the section name and progress, the Monsoon movement turns dark with a scrubbed water rise, and the reduced-motion page is complete and in order. It is accomplished but closer to a familiar premium long-read template, and the column sits narrow inside wide empty margins at 1440px.

why: Both are clean and accessible, but A's draft-mark/waterline idea makes its structure and motion more specific to Jol, while B is the more conventional, if more lavishly typeset, long-read.
